statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

statements.status_notes: Stack buffer overflows in the xmlcatalog interactive shell (--shell) usershell() parser. Still vulnerable in Debian trixie; awaiting an upstream/Debian fix. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11979

Uncontrolled recursion in xmlParseSGMLCatalog reachable only when a local user parses an untrusted SGML catalog with the xmlcatalog CLI. Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible (using untrusted SGML catalogs makes no sense). The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the trixie 2.9.14 source without invasive multi-function changes for a negligible CLI-only issue. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-8732

Stack buffer overflows in the xmlcatalog interactive shell (--shell) usershell() parser. Still vulnerable in Debian trixie; awaiting an upstream/Debian fix. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11979
The libxml2 project reviewed and rejected this report as not a valid security vulnerability; there is no upstream fix to backport. Reference: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/1012

The DHI libxml2 package backports the upstream xmllint interactive shell memory-leak fix from https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/160c8a43ba37dfb07ebe6446fbad9d0973d9279d as dhi-cve-2026-1757-shell-cmdline-leak.patch. Upstream fixes this in shell.c (>= 2.14); the fix is adapted to the xmlShell() loop in debugXML.c on the trixie 2.9.14 source, freeing cmdline before continuing on whitespace-only input. Tracker: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-1757

The DHI libxml2 package backports the upstream xmlcatalog --shell overflow fix from https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/c2e233fc1b341685fc99621b2768b503f777a72e as dhi-cve-2026-11979-xmlcatalog-shell-overflow.patch, which bounds the fixed-size command, arg and argv stack buffers in usershell() and prevents the stack-based buffer overflows. Tracker: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11979

CVE-2026-6732 is a type confusion in libxml2 XSD (XML Schema Definition) streaming validation triggered through xmlParseReference. The harbor-db image uses libxml2 only as a shared library dependency of the PostgreSQL server built with --with-libxml. Inspection of exported symbols in /opt/postgresql/15/bin/postgres and /opt/postgresql/15/lib/pgxml.so shows that no PostgreSQL binary or extension in this image imports any xmlSchema* function or xmlParseReference. Harbor's database schema does not exercise PostgreSQL XML features, and no xmllint or xmlcatalog CLI is present. The vulnerable XSD validation code path is therefore unreachable from any code in this image.
